field_logic.sql: 'Salesforce' AS source_system
field_logic.in_words: Constant per feed.
field_logic.notes: What makes a row traceable once the three sources are unioned.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN record_type IN ('Linear','Digital') THEN record_type
  ELSE 'Unclassified'
END AS platform
field_logic.in_words: Record Type, passed through.
field_logic.notes: The production query overrides this for network "Digital Media"; we dropped that — all seven such rows carry a $0 projection. Record Type is itself a Looker CASE over three literal RECORD_TYPE_IDs plus a date cutoff; build on record_type_name, not the id list.

field_logic.sql: CAST(file_dt AS DATE) AS snapshot_date
field_logic.in_words: FILE_DT — the vintage the row belongs to.
field_logic.notes: Salesforce already snapshots daily. The daily ask is new work for iDeal and Op1, not here.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL                                THEN 'Sports'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.sports_sites)  THEN 'Sports'
  WHEN record_type = 'Linear' AND network = 'NBA TV'              THEN 'Sports'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'                                    THEN 'Digital'
  WHEN record_type = 'Linear'                                     THEN 'Linear'
  ELSE 'Unclassified'
END AS sales_division
field_logic.in_words: Sports if sports_property is populated, or a digital row on SportsSites, or linear on NBA TV.
field_logic.notes: Build this early — lifecycle_state reads it. 14 of the 25 SportsSites entries never appear in these 5,890 rows; that list should be a reference table, not code.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL
    OR forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.sports_sites)
    OR network          IN (SELECT value FROM ref.sports_networks) THEN 'Sports'
  WHEN forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.streaming_bu)
    OR network           IN (SELECT value FROM ref.streaming_bu)   THEN 'Streaming'
  WHEN forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.news_sites)
    OR network           IN (SELECT value FROM ref.news_networks)  THEN 'News'
  ELSE 'Entertainment'
END AS business_unit
field_logic.in_words: A property of the inventory: Sports if sports_property is populated or the site/network is a sports one; Streaming for Max and D+; News for the CNN family; Entertainment for everything else. Will be influenced by allocations
field_logic.notes:
business_unit is OURS and it is a property of the INVENTORY, not of the deal. It reads the network on linear and the site on digital — nothing else — and emits four values: Sports, Streaming, News, Entertainment. There is no Unmapped: anything unrecognised is Entertainment by design.
Neither system supplies it. Salesforce's 'Digital Vertical' is a Looker CASE falling through to DAAP_RPT.UDF_OP_VERTICAL(), a Snowflake function we cannot read, and it returns 'Unknown' on all 3,529 linear rows — not a source field, not carried here. Op1's 'Vertical' IS a real Operative field but its 7 values do not match Salesforce's 9, so neither is the conformed answer.
Deliberately NOT derived from uf_group. uf_group is a sales grouping; business_unit is what the inventory is. Chaining them would let a business unit move because a deal was sold in a different package, which is backwards. The consequence to know: Streaming is Max and D+ only, so WBD Stream inventory takes the business unit of the network it sits on — mostly Entertainment.
KNOWN LIMITATION, not for v1. WBD Stream is a product that can serve on ANY inventory, so pinning it to one business unit is a simplification we are accepting for now. The correct answer is allocation: a WBD Stream opportunity should be split across Max, Entertainment, News and the rest by expected delivery, and each split carries its own business_unit. Until that exists, business_unit mix is directionally right but not exact on this revenue — 411 Salesforce rows / $56.5M and 699 Op1 rows sit in Entertainment when some of the delivery will land elsewhere. This is what allocation_pct and allocation_state are for in the field spec; both ship at a constant 1.0 in Phase 1a. WBD Stream is the concrete case that shows when 1.0 stops being exact.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL
    THEN COALESCE(pm.rolls_up_to, sports_property)
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
    THEN COALESCE(sm.rolls_up_to, NULLIF(forecast_category,''), 'Unmapped')
  WHEN record_type = 'Linear'
    THEN COALESCE(nm.rolls_up_to, NULLIF(network,''), 'Unmapped')
  ELSE 'Unmapped'
END AS property
field_logic.in_words: sports_property through PropMap, then digital sites through SiteMap, then linear networks through NetMap. Anything not in a table keeps its own value.
field_logic.notes: Three lookup tables instead of a forty-branch CASE — the pattern we want for every list.

field_logic.sql:
COALESCE(
  sports_property,
  CASE WHEN record_type = 'Digital' THEN forecast_category ELSE network END
) AS property_detail
field_logic.in_words: The raw value, no rollup.
field_logic.notes: Site-level names live here so property stays clean.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN COALESCE(upf_vs_scat,'') = ''                              THEN 'Unmapped'
  WHEN LOWER(upf_vs_scat) LIKE '%upfront%'                        THEN 'Upfront'
  WHEN LOWER(upf_vs_scat) LIKE '%scatter%'                        THEN 'Scatter'
  WHEN upf_vs_scat IN (SELECT value FROM ref.scatter_vals)        THEN 'Scatter'
  WHEN upf_vs_scat = 'Audience Deficiency Unit'                   THEN 'ADU / Makegood'
  WHEN upf_vs_scat = 'PSA'                                        THEN 'PSA'
  WHEN upf_vs_scat = 'International Sold'                         THEN 'International'
  WHEN upf_vs_scat = 'Programmatic PPM'                  THEN 'Programmatic - Unclassified'
  ELSE 'Unmapped'
END AS market_type
field_logic.in_words: Seven categories out of Classification (UPF_VS_SCAT), anything unrecognised Unmapped.
field_logic.notes: OURS, not a source field. $60.3M lands in Unmapped — almost all linear rows with a blank Classification. That is a data-quality signal, not a bucket to default away.

field_logic.sql: COALESCE(REGEXP_SUBSTR(upf_vs_scat, '[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{2}'), 'N/A') AS upfront_year
field_logic.in_words: Match 25/26 or 26/27 inside Classification, else N/A.
field_logic.notes: Production hardcodes the two year strings, so 27/28 would silently return N/A. Parse the pattern instead, or source a real deal-year field — iDeal has one.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  -- Generic sports MUST come first. Every Salesforce 'Turner Sports' row also carries
  -- sports_property = 'Turner Sports', so a later branch would never be reached.
  WHEN sports_property IN (SELECT value FROM ref.generic_sports)
    OR (record_type = 'Digital'
        AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.generic_sports))
                                                              THEN 'Digital - Sports'
  -- Sports, from sports_property
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL AND record_type = 'Linear'
   AND sports_property IN (SELECT value FROM ref.ncaa_props)  THEN 'Sports Linear - NCAA'
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL AND record_type = 'Linear' THEN 'Sports Linear - Non-NCAA'
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL
   AND sports_property IN (SELECT value FROM ref.ncaa_props)  THEN 'Sports Digital - NCAA'
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL                           THEN 'Sports Digital - Non-NCAA'
  WHEN record_type = 'Linear' AND network = 'NBA TV'          THEN 'Sports Linear - Non-NCAA'
  -- Digital, by site
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category LIKE '%Linear Spon%'                 THEN 'Linear Spon'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.ncaa_sites)      THEN 'Sports Digital - NCAA'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.sports_sites)  THEN 'Sports Digital - Non-NCAA'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.news_sites)      THEN 'Digital - News'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.ss_sites)        THEN 'S&S'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.max_sites)       THEN 'Digital - MAX'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.dplus_sites)     THEN 'Digital - D+'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'
   AND forecast_category IN (SELECT value FROM ref.wbd_stream_sites) THEN 'Digital - WBD Stream'
  WHEN record_type = 'Digital'                                     THEN 'Unmapped'
  -- Linear
  WHEN record_type = 'Linear'
   AND upf_vs_scat IN (SELECT value FROM ref.linear_mkt_types)
                                              THEN 'Linear - ' || upf_vs_scat
  WHEN record_type = 'Linear'                                      THEN 'Linear - Traditional'
  ELSE 'Unmapped'
END AS uf_group
field_logic.in_words: Fifteen values. Generic sports first, then the sports split, then News, S&S, MAX, D+, WBD Stream by site, else Unmapped. Linear splits DDL / Demo Direct / Premiere.
field_logic.notes: Digital - WBD Stream is now POSITIVELY defined. It used to be the digital else and was catching $113.5M, of which $45.6M was CNN and News inventory with nowhere else to go. On Salesforce WBD Stream resolves to The Turner Network alone — DCI ENT, the strongest signal in Op1, does not appear in this extract at all.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN opportunity_stage = 'Cancelled'                          THEN 'closed_lost'
  WHEN projection_rank   = 'F'                                  THEN 'closed_lost'
  WHEN workflow_status IN (SELECT value FROM ref.lost_wf)       THEN 'closed_lost'
  WHEN d.sales_division IN ('Sports','Linear')
   AND opportunity_stage = 'Prospecting/Planning Costs'         THEN 'Prospecting'
  WHEN d.sales_division IN ('Sports','Linear')
   AND opportunity_stage = 'Verbal Commitment/HOLD'             THEN 'Order'
  WHEN workflow_status IN (SELECT value FROM ref.order_wf)      THEN 'Order'
  WHEN workflow_status = 'HOL'                                  THEN 'Pipeline'
  WHEN projection_rank = 'A'                                    THEN 'Order'
  ELSE 'Pipeline'
END AS lifecycle_state

-- d.sales_division is NOT a source column. Compute it in an earlier CTE and join, or
-- repeat its CASE inline. This is the one real ordering dependency in the model.
-- ref.order_wf carries BOTH platform vocabularies (active_order... and ORD). A rule
-- naming only the digital words sends every linear row to the ELSE — that mistake was
-- worth $128.5M in the retired intake draft.
field_logic.in_words: Lost first, then the Sports and Linear overrides, then order workflows across both vocabularies, then HOL is Pipeline and rank A is an Order.
field_logic.notes: Reads sales_division — the overrides fire only on Sports and Linear rows. OrderWF carries both platform vocabularies; a rule naming only the digital words sends every linear row to its else, which is what the retired draft did, worth $128.5M.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN ad_type = 'Placeholder'                      THEN 'Y (Ad Type)'
  WHEN LOWER(opportunity_name) LIKE '%placeholder%' THEN 'Y (name)'
  ELSE 'N'
END AS placeholder_flag
field_logic.in_words: Ad Type first, opportunity name second.
field_logic.notes: Order matters: Ad Type finds 591 rows / $205.8M, the name match 68 / $29.0M, overlapping on 31. Production reporting excludes these in its WHERE clause — we want them carried with a flag so a report can choose.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN LOWER(ad_type) LIKE '%prod%'
     THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS production_fee_flag
field_logic.in_words: Ad Type contains "Prod".
field_logic.notes: Same reasoning as placeholder_flag — production filters these out; carry the flag instead.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN payment_type = 'Barter Trade'
     THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS barter_flag
field_logic.in_words: Payment Type = Barter Trade.
field_logic.notes: Digital rows only in this sample. The field is overloaded — "Programmatic Guaranteed" is a deal type sitting in a payment-type field.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN upf_vs_scat = 'Direct Response'
     THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS direct_response_flag
field_logic.in_words: Classification = Direct Response.
field_logic.notes: 23 rows, all digital.

field_logic.sql:
COALESCE(NULLIF(mega_agency,''), 'INDEPENDENT') AS holdco_conformed

-- SIMPLIFIED. Production resolves holdco through a four-step cascade, and porting
-- those two PI_ tables is the actual ask:
--   COALESCE(dimagency.parentagency,
--            UPPER(sf_mega.mega_agency),
--            pi_agency.rev_agy,
--            agency_name)                       AS holdco_in
--   LEFT JOIN pi_holdco_mapping h ON h.ori_hold = holdco_in  -> h.rev_hold
-- Note it keys on agency_name while iDeal resolves from buying_agency.
field_logic.in_words: The holdco where one resolved,.Needs mapping standardized (not shown as standardized in sample)
field_logic.notes: SIMPLIFIED here. Production resolves it through COALESCE(INSIGHT_DIMAGENCY.parentagency, SF_MEGA_AGENCY.mega_agency, PI_AGENCY_MAPPING.REV_AGY, agency_name) then PI_HOLDCO_MAPPING.ORI_HOLD to REV_HOLD. Those two PI_ tables are the conformed map — port them. Note the chain keys on agency_name while iDeal resolves from buying_agency.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN COALESCE(mega_agency,'') = '' AND COALESCE(agency_name,'') <> '' THEN 'Y'
  ELSE 'N'
END AS holdco_unmatched_flag
field_logic.in_words: Y where an agency is present but no holdco resolved.
field_logic.notes: The point of the default — unmatched revenue stays visible.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN forecasted_value > 0
     THEN ROUND(weighted_scheduled_pipeline / forecasted_value, 4)
END AS probability_pct

-- Carry the raw probability column instead if one exists
field_logic.in_words: Weighted over unweighted.
field_logic.notes: Carry the raw probability column instead. The ratio is a clean ladder (0.00, 0.15, 0.20, 0.65, 0.95, 1.00 cover 98%), which says it is stored upstream.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN d.lifecycle_state = 'Order'
     THEN forecasted_value ELSE 0 END AS booked_revenue
field_logic.in_words: Net Projections where lifecycle_state is Order.
field_logic.notes: $262.5M on this sample.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN d.lifecycle_state IN ('Pipeline','Prospecting')
     THEN forecasted_value ELSE 0 END AS pipeline_projection_net
field_logic.in_words: Net Projections where lifecycle_state is Pipeline or Prospecting.
field_logic.notes: Pass through as exported.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN d.lifecycle_state IN ('Pipeline','Prospecting')
     THEN weighted_scheduled_pipeline ELSE 0 END AS pipeline_projection_weighted
field_logic.in_words: Net Weighted Projections on the same filter.
field_logic.notes: Pass through — never recompute from probability or rank.

field_logic.sql: 'Op1' AS source_system
field_logic.in_words: Constant per feed.
field_logic.notes: Everything in Op1 is digital.

field_logic.sql: 'Digital' AS platform   -- Op1 carries no linear inventory
field_logic.in_words: Constant.
field_logic.notes: Op1 carries no linear inventory.

field_logic.sql:
CAST(<extract_run_date> AS DATE) AS snapshot_date

-- . Retention 13 weeks daily, then thin to weekly.
field_logic.in_words: The vintage the row belongs to — stamped on each daily extract.
field_logic.notes: TO BUILD. Op1 carries no load or effective date today, so this is yours to add. One row per key per day, weekends and holidays included, cut at an agreed time in America/New_York (we propose 06:00 ET so all three sources share a clock). Immutable once written — a correction creates a new day's row, it never edits an old one. Retention: 13 weeks daily, then thin to weekly. Salesforce already does this via FILE_DT, so Op1 and iDeal are where the work is.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.generic_sports) THEN 'Sports'
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL                    THEN 'Sports'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.sports_sites)   THEN 'Sports'
  ELSE 'Digital'
END AS sales_division
field_logic.in_words: Sports if the Site is generic sports, or sports_property is populated, or the Site is on SportsSites. Otherwise Digital.
field_logic.notes: Same shape as Salesforce. Note Op1 sports_property is populated on only 1% of rows against Salesforce's 17%, so the site list still does most of the work here.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL
    OR site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.sports_sites)   THEN 'Sports'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.streaming_bu)   THEN 'Streaming'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.news_sites)     THEN 'News'
  ELSE 'Entertainment'
END AS business_unit
field_logic.in_words: Same rule as Salesforce, on Site — Op1 carries no linear inventory so the network branches do not apply.
field_logic.notes:
business_unit is OURS and it is a property of the INVENTORY, not of the deal. It reads the network on linear and the site on digital — nothing else — and emits four values: Sports, Streaming, News, Entertainment. There is no Unmapped: anything unrecognised is Entertainment by design.
Neither system supplies it. Salesforce's 'Digital Vertical' is a Looker CASE falling through to DAAP_RPT.UDF_OP_VERTICAL(), a Snowflake function we cannot read, and it returns 'Unknown' on all 3,529 linear rows — not a source field, not carried here. Op1's 'Vertical' IS a real Operative field but its 7 values do not match Salesforce's 9, so neither is the conformed answer.
Deliberately NOT derived from uf_group. uf_group is a sales grouping; business_unit is what the inventory is. Chaining them would let a business unit move because a deal was sold in a different package, which is backwards. The consequence to know: Streaming is Max and D+ only, so WBD Stream inventory takes the business unit of the network it sits on — mostly Entertainment.
KNOWN LIMITATION, not for v1. WBD Stream is a product that can serve on ANY inventory, so pinning it to one business unit is a simplification we are accepting for now. The correct answer is allocation: a WBD Stream opportunity should be split across Max, Entertainment, News and the rest by expected delivery, and each split carries its own business_unit. Until that exists, business_unit mix is directionally right but not exact on this revenue — 411 Salesforce rows / $56.5M and 699 Op1 rows sit in Entertainment when some of the delivery will land elsewhere. This is what allocation_pct and allocation_state are for in the field spec; both ship at a constant 1.0 in Phase 1a. WBD Stream is the concrete case that shows when 1.0 stops being exact.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(pm.rolls_up_to, sports_property)
  WHEN property IS NOT NULL AND property <> '' THEN property
  ELSE COALESCE(sm.rolls_up_to, site)
END AS property
field_logic.in_words: sports_property through PropMap first, then Op1's own Property field, then Site through SiteMap.
field_logic.notes: Op1 supplies its own Property, which differs from Site on only 42 of 4,600 rows and every difference is a sports refinement (HBO Max to Turner Sports MM, Turner MLB to MLB, NCAA.com to NCAA.com MM). Salesforce has no equivalent field, so there property is built entirely from the lookup tables — worth knowing the two are not produced the same way.

field_logic.sql: COALESCE(sports_property, site) AS property_detail
field_logic.in_words: sports_property where populated, else the raw Site value.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN COALESCE(classification,'') = ''                        THEN 'Unmapped'
  WHEN LOWER(classification) LIKE '%upfront%'                  THEN 'Upfront'
  WHEN LOWER(classification) LIKE '%scatter%'                  THEN 'Scatter'
  WHEN classification IN (SELECT value FROM ref.scatter_vals)  THEN 'Scatter'
  WHEN classification = 'Audience Deficiency Unit'             THEN 'ADU / Makegood'
  WHEN classification = 'PSA'                                  THEN 'PSA'
  WHEN classification = 'International Sold'                   THEN 'International'
  WHEN classification = 'Programmatic PPM'            THEN 'Programmatic - Unclassified'
  ELSE 'Unmapped'
END AS market_type
field_logic.in_words: Seven categories out of Classification, anything unrecognised Unmapped.
field_logic.notes: Op1 carries a native Market Type field. It is NOT in this sample on purpose. market_type is a dimension WE define, and Op1's version disagrees with Op1's own Classification on 1,228 rows / $123.4M — including 1,000 rows / $93.5M it calls Upfront that Classification calls Scatter. Both fields are order-level and constant within an order, so it is a contradiction rather than a grain artifact. The order naming convention backs Classification in both directions (136 to 1 one way, 6 to 1 the other). Derive market_type from Classification on every system — it is also the field Salesforce uses, as UPF_VS_SCAT.

field_logic.sql: COALESCE(REGEXP_SUBSTR(classification, '[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{2}'), 'N/A') AS upfront_year
field_logic.in_words: Match 25/26 or 26/27 inside Classification, else N/A.
field_logic.notes: Same rule as Salesforce, same field. Hardcoded years should become a pattern parse.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.generic_sports)          THEN 'Digital - Sports'
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL
   AND sports_property IN (SELECT value FROM ref.ncaa_props)   THEN 'Sports Digital - NCAA'
  WHEN sports_property IS NOT NULL                            THEN 'Sports Digital - Non-NCAA'
  WHEN site LIKE '%Linear Spon%'                              THEN 'Linear Spon'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.ncaa_sites)             THEN 'Sports Digital - NCAA'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.sports_sites)            THEN 'Sports Digital - Non-NCAA'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.news_sites)             THEN 'Digital - News'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.ss_sites)               THEN 'S&S'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.max_sites)              THEN 'Digital - MAX'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.dplus_sites)            THEN 'Digital - D+'
  WHEN site IN (SELECT value FROM ref.wbd_stream_sites)
    OR package_name ILIKE '%WBD Stream%'
    OR package_name ILIKE '%Stream+%'                         THEN 'Digital - WBD Stream'
  ELSE 'Unmapped'
END AS uf_group
field_logic.in_words: As Salesforce, plus a package test: a Package Name containing "WBD Stream" or "Stream+" resolves to Digital - WBD Stream.
field_logic.notes:
The package test is the whole point — WBD Stream is a PACKAGE, not a site. 926 rows / $59.0M of WBD Stream packages sit across nine different sites. Do NOT use Product Name for this: its "stream" matches are Instream / Outstream ad formats. Note 255 rows / $18.8M of WBD Stream packages still resolve elsewhere because a site rule outranks them (HBO Max $6.9M, Turner Sports $8.9M, Discovery+ $2.8M) — deliberate, see wbd_stream_package_flag.
sports_property is not the same field on the two systems. Salesforce carries the RAW value (CBB-Big East, March Madness - Digital, Bleacher Report (non-OMP)) on 17% of rows; Op1 carries an already-ROLLED-UP value (MLB, March Madness, College Basketball) on 1% of rows. NCAAProps therefore lists both spellings. On Op1 the field is too sparse to be the main sports signal — the site list still does that work — but it is what catches the 12 March Madness rows sold on HBO Max, which the site test alone reads as Digital - MAX.
KNOWN LIMITATION, not for v1. WBD Stream is a product that can serve on ANY inventory, so pinning it to one business unit is a simplification we are accepting for now. The correct answer is allocation: a WBD Stream opportunity should be split across Max, Entertainment, News and the rest by expected delivery, and each split carries its own business_unit. Until that exists, business_unit mix is directionally right but not exact on this revenue — 411 Salesforce rows / $56.5M and 699 Op1 rows sit in Entertainment when some of the delivery will land elsewhere. This is what allocation_pct and allocation_state are for in the field spec; both ship at a constant 1.0 in Phase 1a. WBD Stream is the concrete case that shows when 1.0 stops being exact.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN package_name ILIKE '%WBD Stream%' OR package_name ILIKE '%Stream+%' THEN 'Y'
  ELSE 'N'
END AS wbd_stream_package_flag

-- Carries the 255 rows / $18.8M that uf_group routes elsewhere because a site rule
-- outranks the package (HBO Max $6.9M, Turner Sports $8.9M, Discovery+ $2.8M).
field_logic.in_words: Y where the Package Name names the WBD Stream product.
field_logic.notes: Carries the $18.8M that uf_group routes elsewhere on site precedence. One of those packages is literally "Cross Channel Title Sponsorship_Video_HBO Max and D+/WBD Stream" — genuinely cross-platform, so the flag is more honest than forcing a single bucket.

field_logic.sql:
CASE
  WHEN sales_stage IN ('Cancelled','Closed Lost')                    THEN 'closed_lost'
  WHEN workflow_status IN (SELECT value FROM ref.lost_wf)            THEN 'closed_lost'
  WHEN d.sales_division IN ('Sports','Linear')
   AND sales_stage = 'Prospecting/Planning Costs'                    THEN 'Prospecting'
  WHEN d.sales_division IN ('Sports','Linear')
   AND sales_stage = 'Verbal Commitment/HOLD'                        THEN 'Order'
  WHEN sales_stage IN (SELECT value FROM ref.closed_won_stages)      THEN 'Order'
  WHEN workflow_status IN (SELECT value FROM ref.order_wf)           THEN 'Order'
  ELSE 'Pipeline'
END AS lifecycle_state
field_logic.in_words: The converged rule with Sales Stage standing in for opportunity_stage. Op1 has no projection_rank.
field_logic.notes: Sales Stage is DIRTY — 13 values including two spellings of closed won (Closed Won 823, Closed/Won 161) plus "0%" (18) and "100%" (15), which are percentages in a stage field. That is why ClosedWonStages is a list. Op1 also carries Booking Status (Pitched / Lost / Booked / Model-Starting Point / Pending YM Approval / Hold) which looks cleaner and is not in Salesforce — worth evaluating as the real source.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN LOWER(order_name) LIKE '%placeholder%'
     THEN 'Y (name)' ELSE 'N' END AS placeholder_flag
field_logic.in_words: Order Name contains "placeholder".
field_logic.notes: Op1 has no Placeholder value in Ad Type/Buy Type, so only the name test is available here — the weaker of the two. On Salesforce the Ad Type test finds 9x more.

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN LOWER(ad_type) LIKE '%prod%'
     THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS production_fee_flag
field_logic.in_words: Ad Type/Buy Type contains "Prod".

field_logic.sql:
CASE WHEN classification = 'Direct Response'

list_desc.SportsSites: Site / forecast_category values that make a digital row Sports.
list_desc.GenericSports: Generic sports inventory that gets the plain "Digital - Sports" value rather than the NCAA / Non-NCAA split. Matched on sports_property OR site.
list_desc.NCAAProps: sports_property values that count as NCAA. NCAA means the March Madness / MML rights business, NOT college sports generally — college basketball and football are Non-NCAA by design. Carries BOTH spellings on purpose: Salesforce sports_property is raw (March Madness - Digital, MMTVE, BRMM), Op1 sports_property is already rolled up (March Madness). Same dimension name, different level.
list_desc.NCAASites: Site values that make a digital row NCAA when sports_property is empty.
list_desc.NewsSites: CNN and Turner News inventory. Before this list existed these rows defaulted into Digital - WBD Stream — $45.6M on the Salesforce sample.
list_desc.SSSites: Social and sponsorship inventory — social, display and production fees.
list_desc.LinearSponMatch: PLACEHOLDER. Any site whose name contains this string is collected into a "Linear Spon" holding bucket rather than classified. These look like a sports nuance we have not worked through — TNT Linear Spon, TBS Linear Spon, truTV Linear Spon, NBATV Linear Spon. Collected so they can be reviewed together and given a real home later. Matched as a CONTAINS, not an exact value, so new ones are caught automatically.
list_desc.WBDStreamSites: Sites that ARE the WBD Stream product. The Turner Network and DCI ENT are 98.2% and 99.8% WBD Stream packages by net revenue in Op1 (note DCI ENT does not appear in the Salesforce extract). Discovery and Discovery Networks are here as generic stream inventory — they are not the D+ product.
list_desc.MaxSites: Sites that resolve to the MAX stream.
list_desc.DPlusSites: Sites that resolve to the D+ stream. ONLY the explicitly plus-branded ones. "Discovery" and "Discovery Networks" are NOT D+ — they are generic stream inventory and sit in WBDStreamSites instead.
list_desc.ScatterVals: Classification values that resolve to Scatter by exact match.
list_desc.LinearMktTypes: Classification values uf_group splits out on linear rows.
list_desc.OrderWF: Workflow Status values meaning an order. Spans both platform vocabularies — linear uses ORD, digital uses active_order and friends.
list_desc.NewsNetworks: Linear networks that are News. business_unit tests this alongside NewsSites.
list_desc.StreamingBU: Networks and sites that are the Streaming business unit — Max and D+ only, matching the uf_group definition of D+. Generic stream inventory (Discovery, Discovery Networks, The Turner Network, DCI ENT) is NOT here: it takes the business unit of the inventory it sits on, which is Entertainment.
list_desc.ClosedWonStages: Sales Stage values meaning closed won. Op1 carries two spellings of the same state — Closed Won (823) and Closed/Won (161) — so this has to be a list, not an equality test.
